passage: Tuesday, 9 p.m. I was away for four days because of a family emergency and the term paper is due Friday. Sarita told me at lunch to write to the professor today, not on the last day. So I did. I said I had been away, said I would need until the following Wednesday, and attached a scan of the travel tickets. I did not make it sound worse than it was. I just wrote what happened and when I would submit. The reply came within the hour: "Thank you for telling me early. Wednesday is fine." I am so relieved I could cry. I still have work to do, but at least it has a date now. Sangeeta

qa.a: Sangeeta attached a scan of the travel tickets.

qa.q: How might the professor see an early, honest request with a date?
qa.a: The professor can trust the reason and plan around it, since Sangeeta wrote early and gave a clear date without exaggerating.

grounding: After a family emergency a student tells the professor early, proposes a date with proof and does not exaggerate, and receives a fair answer.

passage:
The storm had torn half the tin roof off the family house in the village near Barabanki, and Asif had spent two days helping his father shift grain sacks and tie tarpaulins. His lab report for Dr Rajni Verma was due on Thursday, and the college was forty kilometres away.
On Tuesday morning, before anything else, he walked to the one spot near the well where the phone got signal and wrote to her: 'Ma'am, a storm damaged our house on Sunday night and I am needed at home till Wednesday. I have finished half the report. May I submit it on Saturday? I can send photos of the house and a letter from the pradhan.'
He was tempted to add that the whole family was homeless. They weren't; they were staying at his uncle's house next door. He left it as it was.
Her reply came that afternoon: 'Saturday is fine. Photos not needed. Hope everyone is safe.'

qa.q: Where did Asif go to write the email?
qa.a: To the one spot near the well where the phone got signal.

qa.q: Why was Asif tempted to say the family was homeless, and what was he feeling?
qa.a: He was anxious that the request might be refused and was tempted to exaggerate, but chose honesty.

qa.q: What could Asif do to meet the Saturday date?
qa.a: Set aside a few hours each day after the repair work to finish the second half, perhaps asking a classmate for missed notes.

qa.q: How might Dr Verma see Asif's email?
qa.a: Dr Verma sees an early, honest request with a clear date and offered proof, so she trusts it and replies kindly.

grounding: Shows a student after a storm damages the family home telling the professor early, proposing a date with proof and not exaggerating, which earns a fair reply.
